extra.message: POST /ops/bundle/dispatch-thaw-182 passes the request body or blob query parameter directly to pickle.loads(), optionally after Base64 decoding. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can supply a malicious pickle that executes arbitrary commands with the server's privileges.

POST /ops/vault/dispatch-stash-241 incorporates the caller-controlled ref into a filesystem path without containment validation. An operations-token holder can supply ../ components or an absolute path to create or overwrite JSON files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, subject to server filesystem permissions.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/dispatch-shelf-596 joins the unvalidated name query parameter to BASE_EXPORT_DIR and writes the request body there. An operations-token holder can use traversal or an absolute path to create or overwrite any server-writable file with arbitrary contents.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: POST /ops/xml/dispatch-fold-615 parses caller-controlled XML with DTD loading and entity resolution enabled and network restrictions disabled. When lxml is installed and INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN is configured, an authorized caller can cause external entities and DTDs to access server-side resources. The response does not directly return expanded entity contents.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/dispatch-lanefeed-tally-080 logs the complete Authorization header and request body at warning level. Credentials and sensitive manifest data supplied by operations-token holders are exposed to log readers and retained by logging systems without redaction.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /ops/vault/dispatch-stash-241 persists supplied SSNs and card numbers directly into plaintext JSON files. No encryption or masking protects these sensitive values from access through filesystem copies, backups, or other accounts able to read the files.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/dispatch-shelf-596 buffers the entire request body and persists it without a size limit or storage quota. An operations-token holder can exhaust process memory with oversized bodies or exhaust disk space through repeated uploads using different names.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The unauthenticated password-reset request endpoint returns a valid reset token whenever APP_ENV is not exactly production; APP_ENV defaults to local. In that configuration, an attacker can submit any enabled user's email, obtain dev_reset_token, and use the confirmation endpoint to replace that user's password, including an administrator's.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: Password-reset requests append the user's email and raw reset token to local_mocks/password_resets.log. This write also occurs when APP_ENV is production. Anyone with access to this log can use an unexpired token to replace the associated account's password.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Registration hardcodes secure=False when issuing the authenticated session cookie, ignoring COOKIE_SECURE even when enabled for login. Browsers can therefore transmit newly registered users' session cookies over HTTP, exposing them to network interception and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: GET /api/reference returns worker_out() for up to 200 active workers to every authenticated user. The worker query restricts only region-scoped dispatchers; customer accounts, including newly self-registered accounts, receive unrelated workers' names, emails, regions, availability, certifications, and vehicle labels.

route_out() serializes every route job without checking whether the requesting worker remains assigned to it. assign_job() changes assigned_worker_id but preserves the previous route_id when no new route is supplied (lines 834–835). The previous worker can subsequently read reassigned jobs, including internal notes and customer addresses, through GET /api/routes despite failing the normal job ownership check.

CSV exports write user-controlled cell values without neutralizing spreadsheet formulas. A customer can submit an incident customer_summary beginning with '='; export_incidents() includes that value in the CSV. Opening the report in spreadsheet software can evaluate the attacker-supplied formula. CSV quoting does not prevent formula execution.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: Proof uploads are read completely into memory before enforcing the 10 MB limit. An authorized field worker or dispatcher can submit oversized files and exhaust server memory before rejection. read_csv_upload() repeats this pattern at lines 1497–1499, checking its 2 MB limit only after a complete read.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: The public login endpoint verifies every submitted password without tracking failed attempts, applying account lockouts, or throttling requests. No application middleware supplies these controls. Attackers can repeatedly guess passwords or perform credential stuffing against known accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The unauthenticated registration endpoint returns a distinct HTTP 409 response stating that an account exists when the supplied email matches any user. This reveals registered customer and staff email addresses to callers probing candidate addresses.

CSV import catches exceptions and returns their raw string representations to the caller. A dispatcher can submit an invalid job priority to trigger a database constraint exception, exposing SQL statements, bound parameters, and database schema details through the errors response.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: client_ip() trusts the first X-Forwarded-For value from every request without checking whether the peer is a trusted proxy. Clients accessing the API directly can supply an arbitrary address that audit() records as their source IP, falsifying the audit trail.

The live admin account-creation form defaults every new user's password to the public constant TempPass123! and submits it unless the administrator changes it. The backend accepts this password and implements no mandatory first-login replacement. Accounts created with the default, including privileged accounts, are accessible using this known credential.
